result:
I read the pinned checkout and wrote the reader record to the requested path.

**What I found (all evidence is `path:line` from the pinned tree):**

- **The protection under study** is the handling of a decrypted-in-browser attachment (data URI + name) when it is offered as a download/preview: the payload must not become an active document in the PrivateBin origin, and the declared media type must not be trusted. The companion text protection (attachment name inserted as text, not HTML) *is* implemented (`js/privatebin.js:728-760`, `2953-2960`).
- **T1 (M4, deepseek-type)** – `setAttachment` takes `mediaType` out of the data URI verbatim and makes it the Blob type, then points the download link at it (`js/privatebin.js:2764-2785`, `2794`). No allow-list anywhere. Dismissal a solver will use: "the link has a `download` attribute".
- **T2 (M8)** – the `download` attribute is set only when the name is not `undefined` (`2797-2799`). A crafted v2 payload with `"attachment_name": null` passes the `hasOwnProperty` gate (`5046`) and jQuery 3.6 deletes the attribute (`js/jquery-3.6.0.js:2`), leaving a bare same-origin blob link.
- **T3 (M10, mimo-type)** – the editor preview passes the file **name** where the MIME type belongs (`2366-2371`), and `hasAttachmentData()` reports data for any existing attachment element (`2920-2926`), so a type policy written around `setAttachment` never runs on that entry.
- **T4 (M1)** – the legacy version-1 route decrypts attachment and name separately (`5051-5062`); it shares T1's fix site, so I grouped it there. **3 independent groups.**

The output also records the masking relations, four conflicts with must-keep-working behavior (attachment previews, filename round-trip on clone, arbitrary Unicode names, v1 paste readability), 60 minutes of effort, and an explicit `unverified` block — notably that the advisory texts and the two fix commit diffs are **not** in the worktree and no git history was readable (shell disabled), so the media-type reading of the b report is an inference from the truncated summary plus the code.
